verdict: FirstEnergy's revenue rose 9.9% to $4.6 billion on stronger demand, lifting earnings attributable to its shareholders 26% to $557 million, or $0.96 a share.

segments.name: Electric sales
segments.note: Selling electricity to homes and businesses across FirstEnergy's service territories — demand rose with new large-load (data center) customers connecting.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Everything else — service fees and miscellaneous regulated and unregulated revenue.

opex.name: Other operating expenses
opex.note: Running the grid and serving customers day to day — shown net of a $103M credit from deferring regulatory assets, as FirstEnergy's statement nets the two.

opex.name: Depreciation
opex.note: Wear-and-tear on power plants, poles, wires and substations — a big, steady cost for a utility.

opex.name: General taxes
opex.note: Property and other non-income taxes across its multi-state footprint.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $345M, partly offset by $39M of miscellaneous income and $55M of capitalized financing costs (interest regulators let the utility add to its asset base instead of expensing) — a net $251M cost.

takeaways.title: Demand did the lifting
takeaways.text: Revenue rose to $4,557M from $4,148M a year ago as electricity sales grew — FirstEnergy has 7.9 GW of contracted large-load demand in its pipeline.

takeaways.title: Core earnings topped GAAP
takeaways.text: Core (non-GAAP) EPS was $0.98 vs GAAP $0.96 — the 2-cent gap is special items like investigation costs and pension credits. Full-year Core guidance of $2.62–$2.82 was reaffirmed.

takeaways.title: Spending heavily on the grid
takeaways.text: FirstEnergy deployed $4.9B in the first nine months under its Energize365 capital plan, the investment program behind its 6–8% Core EPS growth target through 2030.

oneTimers: Special items added a net $0.02 per share of costs in GAAP results — mainly $18M (pre-tax) of investigation and related costs and reorganization costs, partly offset by net pension/OPEB credits.
Net income in the chart is the consolidated $615M; after the $58M earned by noncontrolling interests, $557M was attributable to FirstEnergy shareholders — the basis for the $0.96 GAAP EPS.

footerNote: Utility layout: fuel and purchased power are the direct-cost block.
